items.title: California Sales Tax Calculator (2026 Updated Rates)
items.subtitle: Calculate combined state (7.25%) and county/municipal surtaxes in California. Instant net-to-gross and gross-to-net reverse calculations for Form 1040 Schedule C and state tax remittance.
items.formulaLatex: \text{Total Sales Tax} = \text{Net Amount} \times (7.25\% \text{ State} + 1.57\% \text{ County Surtax}) = \text{Net} \times 8.82\%
items.formulaExplanation: In California, the state levies a statutory sales tax of 7.25%. County, municipal, and transit tax districts add an average surtax of 1.57%, resulting in a typical effective tax burden of 8.82%. To extract sales tax from a gross invoice: Net = Gross / (1 + 0.0882).

faqs.answer: The statewide base sales tax rate in California is 7.25%. When combined with municipal and county surtaxes (which average 1.57% and cap around 10.25%), the total effective rate paid by consumers typically ranges between 7.25% and 10.25%.

faqs.answer: Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, remote out-of-state merchants must register and remit California sales tax once annual sales into the state exceed $500,000. Once crossed, destination-based tax collection becomes legally mandatory.

faqs.answer: Businesses purchasing wholesale goods intended for resale can present a valid state resale exemption certificate to avoid paying upfront sales tax. The seller must retain this certificate in their records for at least three years to satisfy state audit requirements.

faqs.question: Are SaaS and digital goods taxable in California?
